blocking.issue: Acceptance criterion 3 fails. The section says its table is the complete inventory of in-memory per-Node state, but it leaves out state that this document and its dependencies define. Missing: the State client itself (per-shard pipelined and dedicated connections, per-shard breakers, loaded script SHAs), telemetry export buffers, `/tap` buffers, AI candidate latency averages and cooldowns, the Semantic Cache per-Node concurrency cap, the per-Node first-seen GCRA budget, and the Plugin per-Node key-rate counters. An operator cannot tell from the table what a Node restart loses (for example, breaker state and buffered spans).
blocking.evidence: Line 50: "This table is the complete inventory of in-memory per-Node state; new per-Node state needs a row here before it ships." Line 330 of this document: "Per Node it keeps 2 pipelined connections per shard plus up to 8 dedicated ones ... A breaker per shard opens when ..." (no inventory row). Data plane Bounded resources: "| Post-commit writes, `/tap` buffers | Fixed capacity, dropped with a counter |". AI/LLM gateway Model routing: "`latency` | Ascending time to first token | Node-local decaying average" and "skipping open breakers and cooling candidates". WASM plugin system: "10,000 keys per Policy per Node per minute".
blocking.fix: Add inventory rows, each with a Bound, a Rebuilt from and a Why losing it is safe entry: (1) State client connections, per-shard breakers and script SHAs: bound 2 + 8 connections per shard and 8,192 calls in flight (target); rebuilt by redial and `SCRIPT LOAD`; safe because breakers restart closed and the first failures reopen them within 5 s (target). (2) Telemetry and access-log export buffers: bounded by the exporter queue (Observability); lost spans and logs are counted, while metrics restart as counter resets. (3) `/tap` buffers: fixed capacity; only live tap sessions are lost. (4) AI candidate latency averages, cooldowns and candidate breakers: per `AIModel` candidate; relearned from traffic, with 5% exploration (hypothesis). (5) Semantic Cache embedding and lookup concurrency counters. (6) First-seen budget and Plugin key-rate counters: they refill on start. Otherwise drop the word 'complete'. Dropping it still fails acceptance criterion 3, so adding the rows is the preferred fix.

blocking.issue: The headline global quota accuracy bound says 0% over-admission for 'a Quota'. The glossary defines a Quota as unit requests or tokens, enforced by `quota` or `ai.token-budget`, and token Quotas do overshoot (AI/LLM gateway settlement). The document's own table also allows over-admission with a healthy State Store: the layout-switch row allows 2 × `limit`, and the failover row allows more. The headline number therefore contradicts both its own table and a dependency, so a reader who acts on it will over-promise to tenants.
blocking.evidence: Line 346: "In one Cell with a healthy State Store, a Quota admits at most its `limit` per window, 0% over-admission (target), because each unit is reserved atomically first." Line 364: "| Quota layout switch | Node without the switch signal | Up to 2 × `limit` for one window per such Node ... (hypothesis) |". Pack section 11 glossary: "Quota | A long-window Consumer allowance (unit requests or tokens) enforced by `quota` or `ai.token-budget`". AI/LLM gateway Token Budget: "settlement adjusts the reserving window, possibly past its limit".
blocking.fix: Rewrite the bound as: "For a `quota` Policy (`unit: requests`) in one Cell, with a healthy State Store, no failover and no pending layout switch, admission is at most `limit` per window, 0% over-admission (target). Add L × rate per failover and up to 2 × `limit` per Node lacking the layout-switch signal (hypothesis). Token Quotas (`ai.token-budget`) follow the Token Budget rows. Across R Cells the total is at most R × these (target)." Also align the dropped-refund alert with Observability's `RuralzStateWritesDropped` rule (`rate(...) > 0` for 10m), or propose the 0.1% threshold to Observability as an Open question.

Change the Status column to "503 or 502 (pack 8.10)", or add a note under the table.
